# This part was a bit tricky and we tried a few different approaches before
# this one worked. The important thing is that rsync needs the trailing slash
# on the source, otherwise it copies the directory itself into the destination
# instead of its contents. After that we just print a message.
context:
src="$1"
dest="$2"

# This part was a bit tricky and we tried a few different approaches before
# this one worked. The important thing is that rsync needs the trailing slash
# on the source, otherwise it copies the directory itself into the destination
# instead of its contents. After that we just print a message.
rsync -a --delete "$src/" "$dest"
echo "synced $src to $dest"
why: One useful point buried in four lines of narration.
